title: Airlock deploy cohorts and rollforward scenarios
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook for the "airlock" approach — hold a small, instrumented cohort behind an ingress gate that warms caches and validates model variant behavior before gradual traffic migration. For experiments where KV priming, token-distribution changes, or quantized variant differences are likely to show transient regressions.

High-level goals (what I want to learn in airlock):
- Validate p95 and tail error behavior for new model variant under real short-burst traffic.
- Observe any output-quality regressions (semantic drift) on our golden prompt set.
- Warm KV caches for active clients so subsequent ramp is smoother.
- Verify routing and fallback logic (region affinity, model fallback to variant-lite).

Cohort definitions (practical):
- Gate-0: internal-only (SRE+SEs, 5 hosts) — synthetic steady traffic + canary users. Purpose: infra correctness, metrics smoke.
- Gate-1 (airlock): 0.5% traffic, sticky by client-id cookie; only clients with >=5 daily requests allowed. Run 6 hours minimum.
- Gate-2 (validation): 2% traffic, regional split (us-east, eu-west), soft time-window for peak-off hours. Run 24 hours.
- Gate-3 (ramp): 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 6h windows if signals green.

Traffic progression rules (quick cheat):
- Move to next gate only if:
  - error_rate_in_gate < 0.5% (5xx + obvious model failure patterns) and
  - p95 latency delta <= +30% relative to baseline and absolute p95 < 350ms for short prompts, and
  - golden-set quality: top-1 semantic score delta < 2% (see eval harness), and
  - no unhandled fallback incidents > 1 in last 60 minutes.
- If any threshold breached: pause rollout, hold for 30 min for investigation, if persistent >60 min -> rollback to previous stable variant.

Pinning & rollout config notes:
- Pin config keys that must be updated atomically: model_version, quant_profile, routing_tag. We use feature-flagger to flip model_version at the route-level.
- Always create a dedicated release tag in infra repo (runtime:release/<model>-<sha>) and attach model metadata (quantization bits, device type, fv).
- For private/dedicated customers, we publish a sticky fallback mapping so their SRs don't surprise ops.

KV priming strategy (important):
- Warm using a synthetic primer that replays ~500 representative recent prefixes per active client cohort.
- Primer runs at low concurrency to avoid saturating GPU warmup paths. Track memory & cache hit ratios.
- Expected effect: p95 drop after priming by ~10-20% for multi-turn sessions. If we don't see improvement after 90m, investigate cache eviction patterns.

Observability signals to watch (priority sorted):
1) Error rate (5xx + model-consistency exceptions) by route and client cohort.
2) p95 and p99 token-latency per route.
3) Token output quality regressions (golden-set diffs) — automate run every 30m for Gate-1/2.
4) KV cache hit ratio and hot-kv object churn.
5) Fallback frequency (count of automatic fallbacks to model-lite or CPU path).
6) Cost delta per 1k tokens (for the billing dashboard) — watch sudden jumps.
7) User-visible anomalies (in /alerts slack channel, tag "airlock")

Rollback and rollforward scenarios (practical snippets):
- Fast rollback: flip route model_version back to stable tag; also disable primer traffic; notify SRE and PM; run postmortem template.
- Incremental rollback: split traffic 50/50 between stable and canary while investigating; useful if error pattern is client-specific.
- Rollforward (if everything looks good): increase to Gate-2. Also add scheduled job to run extended quality evals (48h golden-set run).

Preflight checklist (before gating any traffic):
- [ ] model artifact verified in staging (sha, checksum)
- [ ] infra release tag created and uploaded (runtime & docker images)
- [ ] canary dashboards copied and annotated for this release (owner assigned)
- [ ] synthetic primer artifacts ready (list of prefixes)
- [ ] alert playbooks updated (ids in this doc)
- [ ] stakeholders notified: #product, #sre, #cs-rep (emails pinned)
- [ ] backup traffic route and rollback button verified in console
- [ ] legal/security sign-off for any private-customer-affecting change

Notes to self / heuristics I've learned:
- Small noisy clients can skew golden-set metrics. Prefer rolling evaluations by client cohort (top 10 clients separated).
- Quantized variants can produce subtle hallucination changes: watch named-entity stability counts rather than only semantic NLL.
- If p95 increases but quality improves, consider slower rollout with staged cost cap to measure UX tradeoff.
- Don't assume warmup steady-state until priming run completes for at least 2x median session length.

Unresolved questions / followups:
- Need a compact signal for "semantic drift" that scales (Marcus suggested embedding-distance threshold; experiment pending).
- Confirm whether private customers want explicit opt-in to airlock cohorts — Aisha to confirm contract language. (Link: https://jira.company/browse/INF-2310)
- Verify if autoscaler config needs different warm-start profile for Gate-1 workloads (we saw one GPU OOM in last attempt).

Quick action items (who/when):
- Sofia: prepare primer list + run 1 dry-run by Mon 2026-03-15.
- Marcus: create runtime:release tag and PR for canary flip. Target: Tue 2026-03-16.
- Aisha: confirm CS comms for private customers by Thu.

Offline debugging checklist (if something blows up):
- Grab request traces for affected clients (trace ids -> storage).
- Compare tokenization / model inputs between stable and canary for first 3 divergent examples.
- Check kernel selection logs for any kernel fallback events.
- Inspect KV cache hit/miss stream and memory graphs for eviction spikes.

TL;DR (for slack snippet):
Airlock = tiny, sticky cohort to warm caches and validate model variant. Progress through Gate-0 -> Gate-1 -> Gate-2 -> Ramp with strict thresholds (error <0.5%, p95 delta <= +30%, golden quality delta <2%). Primer run required. Rollback fast if persistent anomalies.

End notes: store this doc as ephemeral; copy final checklist to confluence when we finalize the playbook.
